candidates.title: Hardknott Roman Fort
candidates.cite: by Social England, edited by H.D. Traill, D.C.L. and J. S. Mann, M.A. Cassell and Company, Limited, London, Paris, New York & Melbourne, 1902; Public domain; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hardknott_Roman_Fort.png
candidates.place_reason: 306d audit 2026-10-13: the plate IS the real fort (near-square, rounded corners, four corner turrets, gates mid-sides, the PRAETORium and buildings inside - matching NHLE 1009349 / Wikipedia: 114 m external, 105 m internal), and its own 'FEET 0-300' scale bar (461 px = 0.1984 m/px) sizes the drawn 575x562 px fort at 114x112 m - exactly the real size. But the stored fit is 2.293 m/px (8 uniform anchors, resid <=2.26 m, centred ON the site point) = 11.6x the plate's own bar: at it the drawn fort becomes 1320x1290 m and its walls land on the surrounding moor - Butterilket (W), New Crags (N), Pathill Crags (E), Horseshow Crags (S), ~600-700 m out (the OS composite: the drawn rectangle spans the whole sheet while the real small hatched 'Hardknott Castle CAMP (Remains of)' sits by the drawn PRAETORium near the plate centre). The 8 anchors are a 1.29x1.38 km ring placed across the whole sheet, not on the fort. Goodrich class: the centre is right, the size is ~11x off. Document deleted.
